info.title: OpenCapacity API
info.summary: A provider-neutral API for data center capacity queries, demand signals, and subscriptions.
info.description:
Status: draft proposal. No provider implements this API. It is not a product or a
commitment of any data center provider.

A customer describes the capacity it needs as a requirement and uses it in three ways:

- Query: ask whether a requirement can be met. The provider returns a graded answer.
- Signal: record a requirement with the provider as a standing need. The customer can
  amend, withdraw, or delete it.
- Subscription: receive an event when the answer to a requirement changes.

Graded disclosure. Every answer element is one of AVAILABLE, POSSIBLE, UNAVAILABLE, or NOT_DISCLOSED.
Density, cabinet count, power, and timing are returned as bands, and each band is
optional. A provider that returns only a grade per location conforms.

An answer is an indication. It is not an offer, a quote, or a reservation, and it
expires at `validUntil`.

Compatibility rules for clients: ignore unknown properties, treat an unknown Grade
value as NOT_DISCLOSED, and treat any other unknown enumeration value as unknown
without failing.

servers.description: Each provider hosts the API under its own host name.

tags.name: Discovery
tags.description: What the provider supports and which locations it names.

tags.name: Signals
tags.description: Standing statements of need that the customer can amend or delete.

tags.name: Subscriptions

get.description:
Discovery document. It needs no authentication so that a client can find the
token endpoint. It states the conformance classes, the location levels, the
recognized features, and which optional answer elements the provider populates.

get.summary: List the locations the provider names
get.description:
Returns the regions, countries, metros, campuses, and facilities that the
provider accepts in a requirement. A provider can omit campuses and facilities
it does not name publicly.

parameters.name: within
parameters.description: Return only locations inside this location code, for example a country code.

post.summary: Ask whether a requirement can be met
post.description:
Evaluates the requirement and returns a graded answer with one result per
location. The provider does not keep the query as a standing need. To record a
need, create a signal.

The provider can answer at a coarser location level than the one requested. A
location the provider does not serve returns grade UNAVAILABLE with reason
LOCATION_NOT_SERVED. It is not an error.

post.summary: Record a requirement as a standing need

201.description: The signal was stored. Its state is RECEIVED.

put.description:
Replaces the customer-supplied part of the signal. The revision increases by one
and the state returns to RECEIVED. Amending a WITHDRAWN signal makes it active
again. A signal in state CLOSED or EXPIRED cannot be amended and returns 409.

delete.description:
Removes the signal from the API. Later reads return 404, and it no longer
appears in lists. Subscriptions that follow the signal move to state EXPIRED. To
end the need and keep the record, withdraw the signal instead.

This specification does not say what a provider keeps in its own records after a
delete. That is governed by the agreement between the provider and the customer.

post.summary: Withdraw a signal and keep the record
post.description:
Moves the signal to state WITHDRAWN. It is no longer an active need, and it stays
readable and listed until it is deleted. The request has no body. Withdrawing a
signal that is already WITHDRAWN returns it unchanged. A signal in state CLOSED
or EXPIRED returns 409.

Subscriptions that follow the signal receive a `signal.updated` event and no
further answer events while it is withdrawn. Amend the signal to make it active
again.

post.summary: Subscribe to the answer for a requirement or a signal
post.description:
Creates a subscription. With WEBHOOK delivery the state is PENDING_VERIFICATION
until the endpoint echoes the verification challenge. With PULL delivery the
state is ACTIVE at once. The first event after activation carries the current
answer with reason INITIAL.

201.description:
The subscription was created. For WEBHOOK delivery this response is the only
one that contains `delivery.signingSecret`.

put.description:
Replaces the customer-supplied part of the subscription. Set `paused` to true to
stop delivery without deleting the subscription. A change of webhook URL returns
the state to PENDING_VERIFICATION.

204.description: The subscription was deleted. No further events are sent.

get.summary: Read or stream the events of a subscription
get.description:
Returns events in sequence order. Available for every subscription, whatever its
delivery type, for at least `limits.eventRetentionHours` after each event.

A provider can coalesce several changes to an answer into one event. An event
always carries the latest answer, so no change is lost, and the sequence has no
gaps.

With `Accept: application/json` the response is one page of events. With
`Accept: text/event-stream` the response is a server-sent event stream that stays
open. Each server-sent event has the event sequence as its `id` and one Event
object as its `data`. Reconnect with the `Last-Event-ID` header or the `after`
parameter.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Return events with a sequence greater than this value.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: Same meaning as `after`, sent by server-sent event clients on reconnect.

200.description: A page of events, or an open event stream.

post.summary: An event sent to a WEBHOOK subscription
post.description:
The provider sends each event as one POST. Delivery is at least once. De-duplicate
on the event `id` and order by `data.sequence`. Any 2xx response acknowledges the
event. The provider retries other outcomes with increasing delays for at least 24
hours and then moves the subscription to SUSPENDED.

Verify the `OpenCapacity-Signature` header before you trust the body. Its value
is `t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>` where the hex string is the HMAC-SHA256 of
`<t>.<raw body>` keyed with the subscription's signing secret.

To the verification event, respond 200 with the body
`{"challenge": "<data.challenge>"}`.

oauth2.description:
OAuth 2.0 client credentials. The token URL is provider-specific. Read it from
`authentication.tokenUrl` in the capabilities document.

scopes.capacity.signal: Create, read, amend, withdraw, and delete your signals.
scopes.capacity.subscribe: Create, read, amend, and delete your subscriptions and read their events.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Maximum number of items in the page.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: The `pagination.next` value of the previous page.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description:
A client-generated key, unique per intended create. A repeat of the same key
within 24 hours returns the first result and creates nothing.

IfMatch.name: If-Match
IfMatch.description: The ETag of the version you are amending. A stale value returns 412.

ETag.description: Version tag of the resource, for use in If-Match.

Problem.description: The request failed. The body is an RFC 9457 problem document.

TooManyRequests.description: The rate limit or the query quota was exceeded.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before the next request.

Grade.description:
The graded answer used for availability, feature support, and interconnection
presence.

- AVAILABLE (green): the requirement is met or will be met by the date it is needed for service.
- POSSIBLE (yellow): it can be met with conditions, or the provider has to review it.
- UNAVAILABLE (red): it is not met and will not be met by the date it is needed for service.
- NOT_DISCLOSED: the provider does not answer this through the API.

LocationRef.description:
A location in a requirement or an answer. Either a named location at one level,
or an area given as a point and a radius.

AreaLocationRef.description:
Everything within `radiusKm` of a point. A provider that lists `areaLocations`
as false in its capabilities returns 422 with code UNSUPPORTED_LOCATION_LEVEL.
The provider answers an area with one result per named location that it chooses
to report inside the area, or with one result for the area as a whole. It does
not have to reveal where its facilities are.

radiusKm.description: Distance from the center in kilometers.

NamedLocationRef.description:
A location at one level. REGION uses AMER, EMEA, or APAC. COUNTRY uses ISO
3166-1 alpha-2. METRO, CAMPUS, and FACILITY use the provider's own codes, as
listed by `/locations`, for example FR for a Frankfurt metro. A campus is a group
of facilities on one site.

To name a metro without knowing the provider's code, set `scheme` to STANDARD and
send the UN/LOCODE without a space, for example DEFRA.

scheme.description: Applies to METRO only. Absent means PROVIDER.

code.description: The code to send in a requirement. For a metro, a campus, or a facility it is the provider's own code.

standardCode.description: For a metro, the UN/LOCODE without a space. It lets a customer match metros across providers.

PowerUnit.description: kVA and MVA are apparent power. kW and MW are real power.

DensityRange.description:
Power per cabinet as a minimum, a target, and a maximum. Any subset is valid, and
at least one of the three is present. Where more than one is present, min is not
greater than target and target is not greater than max.

minimum.description: The smallest number worth an answer. Absent means only the full count is useful.

Demand.description:
How much capacity is needed. Three forms are valid:

1. `cabinets` and `density`. Total power is derived as the cabinet count times
   the density target, or the max when no target is given, or the min when only
   the min is given.
2. `power`, `cabinets`, and `density`. `power` is the total and `density`
   constrains each cabinet.
3. `power` alone, for a need that is not yet expressed in cabinets.

In form 2 the provider returns 422 with code INCONSISTENT_DEMAND when the total
cannot fit: `power` is greater than count times density max, or less than count
times density min.

powerBasis.description: What `power` measures. IT_LOAD is the power drawn by the equipment. CIRCUIT_CAPACITY is the rated capacity of the circuits.

powerFactor.description: Used to convert between apparent and real power. Absent means the provider's default from the capabilities document.

contiguous.description: True when the cabinets must be adjacent in one space.

FlexibleDate.description:
A point in time at the precision the sender chooses: a day (`2027-06-15`), a
month (`2027-06`), a quarter (`2027-Q2`), or a year (`2027`). A value coarser
than a day is a period. In a request, "needed in a period" means needed by the
last day of the period. In an answer, "available in a period" means available on
some day in the period and no later than its last day. Two values are compared
by the last day of each.

AnswerDate.description:
A date in an answer. A FlexibleDate, or NOW when it is already the case, or
NOT_DISCLOSED when the provider does not give the date through the API. An
absent answer date means NOT_DISCLOSED. It never means now.

percent.description: Cumulative share of the demand needed by this date.

Timeframe.description:
When the capacity is needed. Every property is optional. A requirement with no
`neededForService` states an immediate need. That default applies to requests only.

neededForSale.description: When you need to be able to contract for the capacity.

neededForService.description: When the capacity must be usable. Absent means now.

latestAcceptable.description: The last service date that still works. Absent means `neededForService` is firm.

termMonths.description: Intended length of the commitment in months.

ramp.description: Phased need, in date order. The last step is 100 percent. Absent means the full demand at `neededForService`.

Redundancy.description: Minimum redundancy of the power and cooling systems. A hard constraint when present.

PowerFeed.description: Electrical delivery to the cabinet. A hard constraint when present.

PartyRef.description:
A network, cloud, or other organization to connect to. Give an autonomous system
number where one exists, because names are ambiguous.

InterconnectionScope.description: How close the party must be.

maxRoundTripMs.description: Upper limit on round-trip latency to the party, in milliseconds.

required.description: True for a hard constraint. False for a preference.

Feature.description:
A feature name from the registry, or a provider extension that starts with `X_`.
Registry 1.0: LIQUID_COOLING (any liquid cooling method), DIRECT_TO_CHIP_COOLING,
IMMERSION_COOLING, REAR_DOOR_HEAT_EXCHANGER, PRIVATE_CAGE, PRIVATE_SUITE,
HIGH_FLOOR_LOADING, RENEWABLE_ENERGY_MATCHED, CLOUD_ON_RAMP, INTERNET_EXCHANGE,
REMOTE_HANDS, EXPANSION_OPTION, BUILD_TO_SUIT.

required.description: True for a hard constraint. False for a preference.

CapacityRequirement.description: The capacity a customer needs. Queries, signals, and subscriptions all carry it.

locations.description: Alternatives. The answer has a result for each. Levels can be mixed.

reference.description: Your own reference, echoed in the answer.

CabinetBand.description:
A band for the number of cabinets. `min` alone reads as "at least". `max` alone
reads as "up to". A provider that does not want to reveal inventory returns `min`
no greater than the requested count and omits `max`.

status.description: IN_SERVICE means the capacity exists today. PLANNED means it is expected later.

availableForSale.description: When the provider can contract for the capacity.

availableForService.description: When the capacity is usable. A coarser value discloses less.

required.description: Echo of the request flag, for a feature that was asked for.

availableForService.description: For a feature that is planned.

InterconnectionResult.description:
Whether a party is reachable. Saying that a named party is present discloses
something about that party. A provider grades presence AVAILABLE only for a
party whose presence is already public or that has agreed to be listed, and
NOT_DISCLOSED otherwise.

roundTripMs.description: Band for round-trip latency to the party, in milliseconds.

Reason.description: Why a result is not AVAILABLE.

LocationResult.description:
The answer for one location. Only `location`, `grade`, and `supportedFeatures`
are required. `supportedFeatures` has one entry for each desired feature.

When `grade` is AVAILABLE or POSSIBLE, the entry for each feature that the
request marked `required` is AVAILABLE or POSSIBLE. The location grade already
states that the required features can be met. An entry for a required feature
can be NOT_DISCLOSED only when `grade` is NOT_DISCLOSED or UNAVAILABLE. An entry
for a feature that is not required can be NOT_DISCLOSED with any grade.

location.description: The location answered. It can be coarser than the one requested.

requested.description: The requested location, where the answer is at a coarser level.

density.description: The per-cabinet density the location supports for this requirement.

nextStepUrl.description: Where to continue the conversation with the provider.

validUntil.description: After this time the answer says nothing about availability.

grade.description: The best grade among the results.

SignalState.description:
RECEIVED: stored, not yet taken into planning. ACKNOWLEDGED: the provider has
taken it into planning. WITHDRAWN: the customer ended the need and kept the
record; not an active need. CLOSED: the provider ended it, see `closeReason`.
EXPIRED: `expiresAt` passed. RECEIVED and ACKNOWLEDGED are the active states.

Allowed transitions: RECEIVED to ACKNOWLEDGED. ACKNOWLEDGED or WITHDRAWN to
RECEIVED on amend. RECEIVED or ACKNOWLEDGED to WITHDRAWN on withdraw. RECEIVED,
ACKNOWLEDGED, or WITHDRAWN to EXPIRED. RECEIVED or ACKNOWLEDGED to CLOSED.
CLOSED and EXPIRED are final. Delete removes the signal from any state.

Confidentiality.description: What the provider can do with the signal. Absent values take the most restrictive default.

sharing.description:
NONE: the provider uses the signal only for its own capacity planning.
AGGREGATED: the provider can also include it in totals that do not identify
the customer, for example a load forecast given to a utility.

contactPermitted.description: True when the provider can contact you about the signal. Requires `contact`.

expiresAt.description: Absent means the provider's maximum signal lifetime.

answer.description: The provider's current answer to the signal, where it gives one.

signingSecret.description: Returned once, in the create response.

SubscriptionState.description:
PENDING_VERIFICATION: waiting for the webhook endpoint to echo the challenge.
ACTIVE: events are delivered. PAUSED: stopped by the customer. SUSPENDED: stopped
by the provider after repeated delivery failures; amend the subscription to
return to PENDING_VERIFICATION. EXPIRED: `expiresAt` passed or the followed
signal ended. EXPIRED is final.

SubscriptionRequest.description: Exactly one of `requirement` and `signalId` is present.

signalId.description: Follow the answer and the state of one of your signals.

notifyOn.description: GRADE_CHANGE sends an event when a grade changes. ANY_CHANGE also sends one when a band, a date, or a feature entry changes.

lastSequence.description: Sequence of the most recent event.

sequence.description: Increases by one per event within a subscription.

reason.description: For answer events. REFRESH means the previous answer expired and nothing else changed.

Event.description: A CloudEvents 1.0 envelope in structured JSON mode.

id.description: Unique per event. De-duplicate on this value.

DisclosureLevel.description: How often the provider populates an optional answer element.

specVersion.description: The version of this specification that the provider implements.

conformance.description: CORE covers capabilities, locations, and queries.

locationLevels.description: The levels accepted in a requirement.

areaLocations.description: True when the provider accepts a point and a radius as a location.

finestAnswerLevel.description: The finest level at which the provider answers.

features.description: The features the provider recognizes. Any other feature is answered NOT_DISCLOSED.

disclosure.description: Which optional answer elements the provider populates.

minNotificationIntervalSeconds.description: The provider sends at most one answer event per subscription in this interval. Changes inside the interval are coalesced into one event that carries the latest answer.

next.description: Cursor for the next page. Absent on the last page.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem details with a stable `code` and field-level errors.

pointer.description: JSON Pointer to the field in the request body.
